A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ElChat. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and added experiments in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original adaptation experiments with Qwen2.5 and Llama 3.1, including task performance, inference efficiency, ablations, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds BBH, AlpacaEval, and Qwen3 adaptation results, including detailed appendix tables.

M1.justification: The procedure remains vocabulary expansion and continual pre-training, source–target model merging, and copying special-token weights. v4 expands the operational explanation and notation without establishing a change to the underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: v4 adds English BBH reasoning evaluation and AlpacaEval v2.0 chat evaluation. The adaptation corpus, seven target languages, and previous evaluation datasets remain; Qwen3 uses three already-covered languages.

E2.justification: AlpacaEval introduces comparison against GPT-4 (1106 Preview) reference responses. The existing Base, Chat, CPT, VE, and CV comparison methods remain unchanged. The added CV summary row in Table 2 draws on comparisons already available in v3's appendix.

E3.justification: v4 adds a Qwen3 14B configuration with a 0.1:0.9 source-to-adapted merging ratio and an AlpacaEval win-rate protocol judged by GPT-4.1 nano. Existing Qwen2.5/Llama 3.1 training budgets, sampling settings, and stated few-shot protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds an analysis of whether ElChat's behavior generalizes to a newer, larger model. BBH results also extend the existing Llama component-ablation and linear-merging comparisons. The previous ablations, token-use analyses, and MGSM qualitative examples remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report three runs for summarization and translation, single runs for the listed deterministic evaluations, and 95% confidence intervals in aggregate figures. Added results do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice, increased run count, or statistical test.

E6.justification: Matched existing table values are unchanged, but v4 substantially expands results with BBH, AlpacaEval, and Qwen3 evaluations. Table 10 reports AlpacaEval win rates of 17.16 for Bengali-adapted Qwen2.5 ElChat versus 1.27 for CV. Table 13 reports Qwen3 Bengali GMMLU accuracy of .40 for ElChat versus .58 for Chat, documenting a new adaptation failure.

T1.justification: The new matrix dimensions, SLERP expression, and special-token copying assignments formalize operations already described in v3. They introduce no substantive new mathematical assumptions, theoretical results, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: adaptation without a base model or target chat data, stronger chat/instruction-following and English performance than CV, competitive target-language and safety performance, and retained inference speedups.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a model-specific applicability qualification: stronger prior Bengali/Telugu coverage may explain why vocabulary expansion harms Qwen3 on some target tasks. It also interprets Qwen3's smaller English losses as reduced forgetting. Section 7 expands the interpretation of copying weights relative to CV.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly documents byte-level BPE and selection of non-overlapping frequent tokens. It adds adapted-model access information, Qwen3 templates and model links, MI300X hardware details, and AlpacaEval implementation version 0.6.6. These supplement the substantial implementation information already present in v3.

R1.justification: v4 adds references supporting AlpacaEval, BBH, Qwen3, and Trillion, and explicitly locates ElChat's novelty in combining established components. The related-work organization and positioning against CV remain largely unchanged; publication and citation-format updates do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain. Localized revisions expand Section 3 into a detailed procedural explanation, move embedding initialization there from Section 4.3, elaborate the ablation discussion, and edit the title, terminology, and publication information.

P2.justification: v4 comprehensively changes the two-column document into the TMLR single-column layout and redistributes figures and tables. It adds workflow Figure 2, BBH panels and table columns, and Qwen3/AlpacaEval displays. The inference-efficiency plots and qualitative examples are also rearranged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves procedural clarity and reproducibility information, while the added evaluations expose useful applicability limits, particularly Qwen3's target-language failures. These strengthen an already extensive empirical study. Small reporting errors temper the gain: Appendix C.3 claims a 6.3-point Telugu-to-English improvement, whereas Table 13 gives 47.3 minus 41.6, or 5.7.
